main_issue: The core XXE mechanism is coherent and well supported by several cases, but the guideline is overbroad: it treats XPath inputs and all XSLT processing as equivalent to XML external-resource resolution, while multiple assigned cases provide only patch-location or retrieval-entry evidence rather than source-to-sink proof. The cluster summary also admits unrelated XML mechanisms that should not be covered by this rule.
suggested_guideline: Trace attacker-controlled XML documents or XML-derived inputs into parser, schema, SOAP, or transformer instances that can resolve DTDs or external resources. Flag a path only when the exact instance used for parsing or transformation permits external general entities, external parameter entities, external DTD loading, schema access, or stylesheet/document access, and no effective resolver or external-access restriction is enforced on that path. Verify that the input can contain a relevant external-reference construct and that resolution occurs before reporting. Remediate by disabling DTD and external-entity processing where feasible, setting restrictive external-access properties, and using a rejecting resolver for every parser or transformer instance that processes untrusted XML.
split_suggestions: XXE through insecure XML parser or SOAP/XML utility configuration, including external DTD and entity resolution
External resource loading through XSLT, schema, XPath-related XML utilities, or namespace/document resolution, where a distinct transformer or resolver configuration is the sink
evidence_notes: Allure JUnit and XUnit parsers directly construct default DocumentBuilderFactory/DocumentBuilder instances and parse XML files without an entity-blocking resolver; this is strong direct evidence for the core XXE mechanism.

DBeaver, axmlrpc, java-xmlbuilder, and Bonita cases are CWE-611-associated patch anchors and are plausibly part of the same parser-hardening family, but the payload does not include trace evidence establishing the precise vulnerable parser settings.
Apache CXF Fediz has only hunk anchors and no trace evidence; its inclusion needs confirmation that the changed DOM utility parses untrusted XML with external resolution enabled.

The AWS Android case is labeled SSRF and supplies only review-entry provenance, not exploit or sink evidence. Confirm whether RegionMetadataParser/XpathUtils enables XML external-resource resolution before retaining it.

The HtmlUnit case is labeled template_expression_injection and supplies only a review-entry window around XSLTProcessor.transform. It may belong in an XSLT external-resource submechanism, but the supplied evidence cannot establish that.
The claimed 64 historical examples and the stated 11 assigned cases cannot be assessed from the eight displayed examples; do not use the count as mechanism evidence.
